topics.name: Financial accounting: the double-entry system and verification

questions.q: Which error causes the trial balance not to agree?
o: Transposition in one ledger account only
questions.why: A one-sided error makes total debits differ from total credits.

questions.q: A suspense account is opened when…
o: the trial balance does not agree
questions.why: The difference is held temporarily until errors are found and corrected.

questions.q: A sales ledger control account helps to…
o: check the accuracy of individual customer accounts
questions.why: Its balance should equal the total of the customer (trade receivables) accounts.

topics.name: Financial accounting: adjustments and financial statements

o: the lower of cost and net realisable value
the higher of cost and NRV
more in early years, less later
questions.why: A fixed percentage is applied to the falling carrying value.

questions.q: Accrued expenses at year end are shown as…
questions.why: Money is owed for expenses already incurred.

long.q: A machine cost $50 000 and is depreciated at 20% a year using the reducing balance method. Calculate the depreciation for years 1 and 2 and the net book value at the end of year 2.
scheme: M1: net book value after year 1 = $40 000

long.q: Trade receivables are $40 000. The allowance for irrecoverable debts is to be 5% of trade receivables; last year's allowance was $1500. Calculate the entry in the income statement and the net figure shown in the statement of financial position.
scheme: A1: increase of $500 charged to the income statement

topics.name: Financial accounting: partnerships and limited companies

questions.q: If a partnership agreement is silent, profits are shared…
questions.why: Default rules apply when there is no agreement.

questions.q: Share premium arises when shares are issued…
questions.why: The excess over nominal value goes to the share premium account.

long.q: A and B are partners. A's capital is $50 000 and B's $30 000. Interest on capital is 5%, B receives a salary of $10 000, and remaining profits are shared 3 : 2. Profit for the year is $60 000. Prepare the figures for the appropriation account.
scheme: M1: interest on capital: A $2500, B $1500

questions.q: Trade receivables turnover in days is…
questions.why: It shows how long customers take to pay.

o: the proportion of capital financed by long-term debt
questions.why: Highly geared businesses carry more financial risk.

long.q: A business has revenue of $200 000 and cost of sales of $140 000. Calculate its gross margin and its mark-up.

o: selling price − fixed cost per unit
selling price − variable cost per unit
questions.why: Contribution covers fixed costs, then gives profit.

questions.q: In absorption costing, overheads are absorbed using…
questions.why: For example, per direct labour hour or machine hour.

long.q: A firm with spare capacity is offered a one-off order for 500 units at $15 each. The variable cost is $11 a unit and fixed costs are already covered. Advise whether to accept, with one non-financial factor.
scheme: A1: total contribution = 500 × 4 = $2000, so profit rises: accept
B1: one non-financial factor, e.g. regular customers may ask for the same low price
B1: or the order may lead to future business / uses idle staff

questions.q: A statement of cash flows classifies cash flows under…

o: a business is bought for more than the fair value of its net assets
questions.why: It reflects reputation, customers and other unrecorded value.

questions.q: A favourable materials price variance means…
questions.why: Actual price below standard price saves money.

questions.q: A project's NPV is positive. This means…
o: it earns more than the cost of capital
it pays back in one year
questions.why: Discounted inflows exceed outflows at the chosen rate.
